operations.description:

Security is maintained through permission checks, and actions are logged immutably for regulatory, audit, and explainability compliance. This endpoint is typically consumed by model management pipelines and admin/operator UIs before initiating training or model retraining workflows.

Failure scenarios include duplication, missing required fields, or model linkage errors, all of which return detailed error messages with evidentiary context for compliance and debugging. Related API operations include PATCH for listing/searching datasets, PUT for updates, and DELETE for removal/revocation.

     */

     * Human-readable dataset name. For analytic description and
     * distinguishability in dataset registry and compliance logs.

    name: string;

     * Version label. Required for evidence traceability, model
     * reproducibility, and audit/version management.
     */
    version: string;

    /**
     * URI to data in external storage (e.g., S3, GCS), required to satisfy
     * evidence preservation and provenance demands in regulatory/ML
     * workflows.
     */

    /**
     * Cryptographic hash of the dataset's schema, enabling integrity
     * checking and compliance evidence. Ensures drift detection and
     * structure non-repudiation.
     */
    schema_hash: string;

    /**
     * Optional. Atomic count of records in dataset, for reporting, audit
     * logs, and ML pipeline sizing.
     */
    record_count?: (number & tags.Type<"int32">) | null;
  };

  /**
   * Patch/update information for an AI training data entity. Fields are all
   * optional, as update logic is partial/mutable only on select fields and
   * only as per compliance and regulatory evidence protocol. See
   * IAiTrainingData for main entity description.

    /**
     * Optional association/update for the AI model reference linked to the
     * dataset. Setting this supports improved lineage and evidence
     * reporting.

    ai_model_id?: (string & tags.Format<"uuid">) | null;

    /**
     * Optional update to dataset name. Enables audit or correction in the
     * AI registry if required.
     */

    /**
     * Optional update to dataset version label. Used for regulatory
     * corrections or evidence drift management.

operations.description:
This API operation enables the registration of a new AI training dataset in the ai_training_data table, as part of the AdvancedAI module. The ai_training_data table is dedicated to cataloguing all datasets—internal or external—utilized during AI/ML model training. This operation allows administrators or automated pipelines to create a new dataset entry, recording metadata such as name, version, source_uri, schema hash, record count, and its association to a specific model (optional).

Upon POST, the system will validate the uniqueness of the combination (name, version, source_uri) to avoid redundant records. If associated with an AI model, it checks referential integrity with the ai_models table. Required fields must be present, and audit/evidence records will be generated for traceability.

Security is maintained through permission checks, and actions are logged immutably for regulatory, audit, and explainability compliance. This endpoint is typically consumed by model management pipelines and admin/operator UIs before initiating training or model retraining workflows.

Failure scenarios include duplication, missing required fields, or model linkage errors, all of which return detailed error messages with evidentiary context for compliance and debugging. Related API operations include PATCH for listing/searching datasets, PUT for updates, and DELETE for removal/revocation.

Evidence of deletion and historical change control is maintained indefinitely for audit.

This operation is related to POST for creation, PUT for updates, and PATCH for search/listing of AI training data.

The submitted data is validated for type, masked detail (never sensitive information), activation status, and optional provider. On success, the new payment method is added to the user's set of available payment options. This operation is critical for maintaining modular payment infrastructure, PCI compliance, and supporting extensibility for new payment methods.
operations.description:
This API registers a new payment method for the authenticated user, storing atomic instrument data such as type (e.g., VISA, wallet), masked details (PCI-compliant), provider, and activation flag. No sensitive credential information is ever recorded—only safe display details. Input must be fully validated (instrument type, uniqueness per user, provider, etc). The method becomes immediately available for checkout, discount/voucher association, and analytics. All changes are audit-logged with user ID and timestamp for compliance.

The operation ensures extensibility and compliance by supporting new method types, audit trails for evidence preservation, and strict separation of user identification from credential data. PCI DSS requirements are enforced, including non-repudiation and rollback protection for registration steps. Errors are returned for duplicate, invalid, or non-compliant submissions.

Related operations: GET/PATCH/PUT/DELETE paymentMethods for managing and auditing existing records.

**Review of Draft E2E Test Function for Audit Log Update**

**Strengths:**
- The plan covers both positive (allowed field update) and negative (forbidden fields, nonexistent ID) test cases.
- Business context and compliance rationale for field mutability are well-stated.
- Proper use of dependency (create record before update).
- Random UUIDs and JSON context for robust data.
- Use of TestValidator.error for runtime (not compile-time) forbidden updates.

**Required Improvements:**
- For negative tests covering forbidden fields: since the update SDK body only accepts IUpdate fields (evidence_archive_id, context), TypeScript would not allow `forbiddenPayload as any` in a type-safe way. The scenario draft uses a type bypass, but such tests cannot be implemented in type-safe TypeScript. Therefore, skip the compile-time impossible cases—only attempt runtime-possible validation (try to update with just allowed fields or empty payload, not forbidden property injections).
- For runtime tests, do NOT use non-existent properties (`id`, `created_at`) in the update payload.
- Ensure error tests only cover what the backend can actually receive and reject at runtime (bad values for allowed fields, not new properties).
- Add a test for partial (empty) update payload (should be valid - possible backend interpretation: no fields actually change).
- Ensure type assertions after response and explain assertion logic.

This operation deletes a single Personalization Event in the favorites and personalization module, identified by its unique ID. The Personalization Event table logs user interactions with recommendations for evidence, AI learning feedback, and compliance/traceability. Deletions are typically soft (setting a deleted_at timestamp) for audit, evidence, and compliance purposes. This operation provides traceable, reversible record removal for privacy (GDPR) or correction processes, ensuring all deletions are logged.

The operation references the Prisma table `personalization_events` (FavoritesPersonalization namespace), which captures all user personalization actions and is linked to audit compliance requirements.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows administrative or user-initiated deletion of a single personalization event by unique ID. Instead of removing physical records, it performs a compliant soft-delete, updating the deleted_at field in accordance with regulatory evidence preservation and data subject rights like GDPR erasure or logistical clean-up.

Deletion is only allowed for users with appropriate authorization, with strict validation of ID existence and referential integrity. Upon deletion, an immutable audit record is created in personalization_audits detailing the action, user, and evidence for later review. The operation ensures no associated data loss for AI training, as delete actions are part of compliance logs and may be factored into model retraining algorithms.

Error cases like non-existent IDs, insufficient permissions, or foreign key constraint violations must return actionable error messages and evidence context for compliance. Related endpoints: GET/PUT/POST for this entity, PATCH for list/search.

Failure scenarios include duplication, missing required fields, or model linkage errors, all of which return detailed error messages with evidentiary context for compliance and debugging. - The code follows TypeScript standards and respects the type safety of input DTOs.
- Compiles successfully if all imported utilities exist.

### Framework Compliance
- Follows the deterministic structure expected for E2E API tests.

- Utilizes `TestValidator.error()` for negative scenarios.

### Data and Edge Cases
- Random UUID generated for campaign ID.
- Both 'percentage' and 'fixed' types validated, including with negative value edge case.

### Readability & Maintainability
- Variable names are descriptive and reflect entity meaning.
- Comment style and workflow are clear and easy to follow.
- JSDoc provides a comprehensive overview of the scenario logic.

### Issues/Notes
- TypeScript won't allow required field omission, so that specific runtime validation cannot be performed unless type safety is bypassed.

2. 성공 시나리오: 모든 필드 포함한 캠페인 정상 생성. 필드 assert로 정확성 검증.
3. 필수값 누락, 날짜 오류 등 validation error에 대해 TestValidator.error()로 런타임 검증 구현.
4. 중복 이름/스케줄 등 비즈니스 규칙 충돌에 대한 에러 처리도 실제로 API가 거부하는지 체크.
5. 실제로 생성된 캠페인의 name/active 등 주요 필드를 별도 assert로 정밀 확. 
6. 모든 타입 할당 및 API 호출 패턴, assertion이 타입 안전성 있게 작성됨.

지키고 있는 점:
- 타입 위반 없는 strictly typed 통신
- 현실적이고 적절한 랜덤/유효값 생성
- 설명/코멘트 체계적
- 단계별 의도 명확

아쉬운 점:
- campaign의 discount_rule 연결 로직은 명시적으로 존재하지 않음 (입력 타입에 campaign_id 없음)
- 실제 룰-캠페인 연결 validation 테스트는 룰이나 캠페인 API에서 추가 구현 필요

최종적으로, 실제 비즈니스 운영상 캠페인 생성에서 발생할 수 있는 다양한 에러/성공 플로우가 광범위하게 커버된 견고한 테스트 코드.

**Strengths:**
- The planned steps explicitly cover filtering (by transaction, user, date, status), pagination checks, invalid parameter cases, and access control for multiple user roles, including unauthenticated access – all reflecting robust E2E coverage for this endpoint.
- Recognizes the need for different authentication contexts (admin, user, unauthenticated).

- Example bad-case parameters should be shown and checked per error type.
- Use the SDK to switch auth tokens for each role, and explicitly clear Authorization for unauth test.

- Ready for implementation, provided setup data and role switching is handled robustly. Add clear success/failure asserts at every step.

operations.specification: Create a new API access token for an API client. Associated with the api_tokens table in the Prisma schema, this operation allows provision of secure, time-limited, and scope-bound tokens needed for authenticated access to the backend's omnichannel API services. Tokens must be securely generated, assigned to an API client, and have their initial lifetime, scope, and permissions validated. All token issuance actions must be logged for compliance and audit. Permission and input validation is mandatory to avoid unauthorized registration.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows authorized clients or system administrators to create and register a new API token, providing the required data for association with a specified API client. The request will validate that the target client exists and is active, ensuring the issued token's scope fits within permitted boundaries (as defined in the permission and policy registries). The returned token is securely generated, not stored or transmitted in plain text beyond initial creation, and set with a defined expiry date.

All operations are centrally audited via the api_audits table for compliance and security event monitoring. The request body must contain all required token metadata and reference to the related API client. Errors in request data, invalid client status, or policy violations will result in a descriptive error response. Sensitive credentials are never logged.

This operation is directly traceable to the api_tokens, api_clients, and policy tables within the database schema. It must check any legal or regulatory requirements (e.g., OAuth, PCI-DSS) during provisioning.

event.scenario: Test issuing a token for a valid client and verify it appears in subsequent token lists. Attempt to issue a token for a non-existent client or with invalid payload to ensure validation and error reporting.
event.review:
Review for the drafted E2E test function:

1. **Correct Business Workflow:**
   - The test first registers a valid API client, issues a token for that client, and asserts properties.
   - It then attempts negative cases: issuing token for a non-existent client and submitting an invalid payload.

2. **Type Safety:**
   - Uses proper typings (IApiClients.ICreate, IApiToken.ICreate, etc.) for all requests and responses.
   - Uses typia.assert on all actual API responses; TestValidator for validation and error cases.

3. **Assertions:**
   - Validates token fields match expectations using TestValidator.equals.
   - Error cases test fail for non-existent clients and missing required fields.

4. **Random Data:**
   - Uses RandomGenerator for client and token data to ensure uniqueness and realism.

5. **Negative Case Type Safety:**
   - In negative test for invalid payload, a type violation is used (`as any`). According to our guidelines, we should only use valid, type-safe values for negative cases and test business logic errors, not schema/TypeScript errors that would not compile. Thus, the invalid payload error scenario that relies on a missing required property should be omitted.

6. **Function Naming, Documentation, Structure:**
   - Function name, documentation, and comments conform to code generation requirements. Implementation is step-by-step, with business logic annotated.

**Action:**
- For final, remove the invalid schema negative test (step 4) as it violates compile-time type safety.
- All other business error/validation logic remains.
- Ensure type assertions and runtime business validations only.
- Finalize with clean docstring and type-safe, type-compliant code only.

The draft implementation:
- Follows all prescribed E2E test steps, beginning with creation, then a valid mutable field update, followed by invalid/forbidden field attempt.

- Correctly asserts invariants for original immutable fields.

For error assertion, keep this as commented illustration but do not include invalid types; focus only on cases that are type-valid but business-invalid (e.g., mismatched created_at timestamps).
- Defensive note: Ideally our negative scenario should validate runtime business rules, not type system or model incompatibilities.

Other notes:
- Test also verifies that update does not remove core evidence (no loss of id or created_at), which is compliant.

Conclusion: The draft represents all required test steps, covers both positive and negative flows, and business validation.

이 코드는 제품 미디어(primary key는 id) 레코드의 수정(갱신) 엔드포인트에 대한 E2E 테스트(유닛+통합)를 구현하였다.

- 시나리오는
  1. 정상 레코드 생성
  2. 정상 갱신(URI/alt_text)
  3. alt_text(접근성 필드) 빠진 상태에서 업데이트 시도 -> 에러 메시지 및 400 확인
  4. 유효하지 않은 id로 갱신 시도 -> 404 에러 발생 검증

- 주요 검증: typia.assert 통한 타입체크, TestValidator를 통한 응답 값/오류 코드 검증
- props 파라미터 타입, API 응답 등 strictly 타입 준수
- Edge case: alt_text 미제공, 존재하지 않는 id 갱신 모두 비정상 에러 발생 여부 체크

추가 테스트로 locale, media_type 등에 대해 수정 시도와 각 validation rule에 대한 에러 시나리오를 확장할 수 있으나, 본 코드는 핵심 시나리오에 집중함.

각 단계는 한글로 비즈니스 로직 목적을 명확히 주석으로 달았고, 이름/설정 등은 실제 DTO/엔드포인트 명세와 100% 일치된다.

event.review:
# 코드 리뷰

## 1. 타입 및 의존성 검증
- 모든 API 응답(생성, 삭제)에 typia.assert() 호출되어 타입 검증 철저
- TestValidator.equals, TestValidator.error 등 주요 비즈니스 검증 포인트 사용 적합
- 예시에서는 제품 연결 미디어 및 상세 조회/검색 API 불명확해 해당 부분 skip했으나 실제 구현 시 추가 필요

## 2. 정상/비정상 흐름 커버리지
- 정상 생성 → 정상 삭제
- 삭제 후 추가 삭제(idempotency/state error 확인)
- 잘못된(존재하지 않는) UUID에 대해 에러 검증
- (추가적으로 참조 무결성 및 상세조회 불가 검증은 정책/값에 따라 일부 skip)

## 3. 코드 구조 및 주석, 명료성
- 각 단계별 주석 및 한글 설명 우수, 시나리오 맥락 명확
- 불필요한 임포트 없이 함수 내부에서만 구현
- 변수명 및 API 함수 파라미터 정확히 매칭

## 4. 누락/개선점
- 상세조회/검색 미디어 검증(존재 불가성)은 해당 API 정의 필요
- 실제 referential constraint 테스트(제품 연결 미디어 삭제 불가 등)는 정책 명시 필요
- 생성 input의 URI 등은 실제 환경에 맞게 적절히 랜덤화 혹은 유효값 생성 필요

# 종합 의견
- 시나리오의 핵심 요구(soft-delete/idempotency/error handlng)는 제대로 반영됨
- 비즈니스/기술 정책에 따라 일부 보완 여지 있으나, 현재 공개 API로는 요구 범위 내에서 적정하게 구현됨

Retrieves paginated and filterable stock/inventory entries. Each entry covers a single product variant's stock level, managed entirely within the 'inventory' table per schema. This operation is foundational for supply chain, logistics, and dynamic AI-powered stock optimization, and downstream integration with catalog, cart/order, and analytics modules.

Security/permissions restrict search to authorized supply chain, warehousing, AI monitoring, or admin users (enforced via RBAC). Search supports filtering on variant_id, stock range, and last-modified timestamps, providing full audit evidence/logging at each access for compliance.

operations.specification: Create a new inventory record. This operation is associated with the `inventory` table in the ProductCatalog schema. It allows creation of an inventory entry tied to a specific product variant, tracking the current stock count and the latest modification timestamp. The operation ensures 3NF compliance by only storing atomic details—one-to-one mapping between inventory and product_variant. Fulfillment of this API is essential for enabling accurate stock tracking, compliance with evidence preservation requirements, and supporting downstream logic (e.g., product availability, order limits). On creation, all business logic for stock adjustment, initial synchronization, and compliance must be enforced. Write-once (create) policy guarantees that all inventory insertions preserve evidence for audits, analytics, and legal traceability.
operations.description: This endpoint enables the creation of a new inventory record in the shopping mall’s product catalog system, referencing the `inventory` table in Prisma. The inventory record is tightly bound to a product variant, establishing one-to-one mapping. All insertions must validate the presence of a valid product_variant reference, prevent duplication for a variant, and enforce atomic storage of stock count and present timestamps. Security controls must ensure only authorized operators or system components may create new inventory entries. The request body should capture the product_variant_id and initial stock_count, and business logic must check for referential integrity. On success, a new immutable inventory record is created; any errors arising from duplication, constraint violations, or invalid references must be returned with clear diagnostics. This operation complements the update (PUT) and delete endpoints for the same resource; evidence of all creation attempts must be logged for compliance purposes.

   * The unique identifier for this inventory record. References the primary
   * key in the inventory table. Essential for traceability, reference
   * integrity, and evidence preservation.
   *
   * See Prisma schema: inventory.id
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The ID of the product_variant this inventory entry is associated with.
   * This ensures a strict 1:1 relationship (see @@unique constraint in
   * schema) and enables accurate stock tracking per SKU.
   *
   * See Prisma schema: inventory.product_variant_id
   */
  product_variant_id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The present available quantity of stock for this specific product
   * variant. Critical for all commerce, fulfillment, and analytics workflows.
   * Always an atomic integer value; never computed in the DB layer.
   *
   * See Prisma schema: inventory.stock_count
   */
  stock_count: number & tags.Type<"int32">;

  /**
   * UTC timestamp indicating when this inventory record was last updated.
   * Required for audit, compliance, and real-time monitoring workflows.
   *
   * See Prisma schema: inventory.last_modified_at

   * only.

     * Business logic should handle initial sync/evidence recording.
     *
     * See inventory.stock_count
     */
    stock_count: number & tags.Type<"int32">;

     * UTC timestamp for when this inventory record is created/set. If

     * evidence preservation.

    last_modified_at?: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
  };

import { tags } from "typia";

import { IProductCatalogProductVariant } from "./IProductCatalogProductVariant";

/**
 * Represents a single, atomic inventory record for a product variant. Fulfills
 * the evidence/logging/integrity requirements described in the Product Catalog
 * Management module of the requirements analysis and in the inventory Prisma
 * schema table.
 *
 * All stock management must operate on these normalized, immutable records.
 * Each inventory state update must be evidence-traced via external logs or join
 * to catalog_events.
 *
 * This type is critical for compliance, audit, analytics, dynamic pricing, and
 * real-time availability.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IInventory = {
  /**
   * The unique identifier for this inventory record. References the primary
   * key in the inventory table. Essential for traceability, reference
   * integrity, and evidence preservation.
   *
   * See Prisma schema: inventory.id
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The ID of the product_variant this inventory entry is associated with.
   * This ensures a strict 1:1 relationship (see @@unique constraint in
   * schema) and enables accurate stock tracking per SKU.
   *
   * See Prisma schema: inventory.product_variant_id
   */
  product_variant_id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The present available quantity of stock for this specific product
   * variant. Critical for all commerce, fulfillment, and analytics workflows.
   * Always an atomic integer value; never computed in the DB layer.
   *
   * See Prisma schema: inventory.stock_count
   */
  stock_count: number & tags.Type<"int32">;

  /**
   * UTC timestamp indicating when this inventory record was last updated.
   * Required for audit, compliance, and real-time monitoring workflows.
   *
   * See Prisma schema: inventory.last_modified_at
   */
  last_modified_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;

  /**
   * Reference to the related product variant object. Provides full details of
   * the SKU/configuration this inventory is managing.
   *
   * Not stored as a column in inventory; included for API response embedding
   * only.
   */
  variant?: IProductCatalogProductVariant;
};
export namespace IInventory {
  /**
   * Payload for creating a new inventory record. Maps to IInventory but omits
   * the server-generated id and focuses on user/system-supplied fields
   * (product_variant reference, initial quantity, timestamp).
   *
   * All creations must match the 1:1 variant/inventory relationship and are
   * logged for compliance.
   */
  export type ICreate = {
    /**
     * References the product_variant for which to create this inventory
     * record. Must point to a valid, existing variant and follows 1:1
     * constraint.
     *
     * See inventory.product_variant_id
     */
    product_variant_id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

    /**
     * Initial available stock quantity for this variant at the time of
     * creation. Must be a positive or zero integer, never negative.
     * Business logic should handle initial sync/evidence recording.
     *
     * See inventory.stock_count
     */
    stock_count: number & tags.Type<"int32">;

    /**
     * UTC timestamp for when this inventory record is created/set. If
     * omitted, system will default to now. Required for consistency and
     * evidence preservation.
     *
     * See inventory.last_modified_at (set to now by default)
     */
    last_modified_at?: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
  };
}

- **Test setup is complete and realistic:** The test first creates a valid notification as prerequisite, ensuring a real, updatable record for the success test path. This matches actual user/data flows.
- **Type safety:** All API calls use exact, type-safe DTOs. No use of `any`, `as any`, or type suppression. Variable typings match DTO signatures.
- **Random data generation:** For user_id and IDs, uses format-tagged random UUIDs. This prevents ID format errors and simulates realistic records.
- **Business logic:** 
  - Update covers all mutable fields (`content`, `notification_type`, optionally `archived`, `read_at`).
  - Change values to ensure the update is meaningful, not idempotent.
  - Asserts that each persisted field matches the intended change.
- **Error handling:** Includes a negative test (update with non-existent ID) and expects/validates a failure via TestValidator.error. 
- **Flow/comments:** Each step is clearly commented, guiding maintainers through logic. Function docblock explains purpose and steps in detail.
- **No skipped logic:** All core scenario requirements are mapped to code.
- **No external dependencies:** Code is self-contained, needs only the standard test infra and imported DTOs/functions.

## Final Verdict
This code thoroughly tests the update endpoint per provided scenario. Clear, type-safe, realistic, and easily maintained. Ready for production E2E usage. All requirements satisfied.

3. **실제 데이터 흐름**: 생성된 알림의 실제 ID를 기준으로 soft delete 및 idempotent/예외 상황까지 일관성 있게 시나리오 전개.

This operation corresponds to the 'reviews' table in the Prisma schema and allows users to submit new review entries, which are subject to AI-powered moderation and sentiment analysis. The endpoint enforces evidence preservation, versioning, and compliance with regulatory and audit requirements. The request body must include review content, language code, verified purchase indication, parent review (if applicable), and product reference. Business logic ensures proper linkage to products/users and triggers sentiment/model analysis and notification workflows. Permissions are required; user actions are fully traced. Error handling covers validation, consistency, and access control.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables creation of a new product or service review. It saves atomic evidence including content, language, product, user information, and verified purchase flag while triggering downstream AI moderation and sentiment analysis. Each submitted review is versioned for full audit support and regulatory evidence. Reviews are typically linked to user and product, preserved and versioned for edit history and moderation, ensuring compliance with privacy, tampering, and content guidelines.

Security: Only authenticated users may create reviews, with full audit trail capture. Review content is eligible for automated analysis and moderation. The endpoint returns created review information upon success, or provides detailed validation and authorization errors as needed. Related moderation or sentiment workflows are triggered upon creation.

Error handling includes duplicate check, input validation (content, language, flag), and evidence tracing for compliance. Edge cases like non-existent target product/user or duplicate reviews are strictly rejected and audited.

operations.specification: Implements the update operation for an existing review, identified by its unique ID, in the communication/review module. Corresponds directly to the 'reviews' table in the Prisma schema. Allows modification of review content, language code, or metadata, retaining full audit/versioning (no hard overwrites). Supports only authorized user or moderator actions, triggers evidence versioning and may initiate AI moderation/sentiment analysis re-execution. Validates review ownership, review presence, integrity, and ensures compliance/auditable trace. Updated review is returned with full revision information.
operations.description:
This endpoint provides secure, evidence-preserving updates for an existing review, as identified by the supplied unique ID. The update operation retains full historical and versioned audit evidence, never physically overwriting prior versions, thus enforcing regulatory and tamper-evidence requirements. Supported modifications include review content, language, or certain editable metadata, subject to ownership or moderator permission. AI-powered sentiment analysis and moderation workflows may be retriggered on update events, with new versioning generated as appropriate. All modifications are logged, and improper updates (e.g., to archived or non-existent reviews) are thoroughly validated and rejected.

/**
 * Validate soft-deletion of user profile with audit/evidence preservation and permission enforcement
 *
 * This test scenario covers:
 * 1. Normal soft-deletion of a user profile (using `eraseById`), ensuring the returned evidence (deleted_at and ID) is present
 * 2. Post-deletion, confirm that fetching the profile (with same or insufficiently privileged user) is rejected or indicates non-accessible
 * 3. Attempting to soft-delete a non-existent profile returns the correct business error
 * 4. Attempting to soft-delete as an unauthorized (insufficient permission) actor results in correct permission error
 *
 * Detailed Steps:
 * 1. Create a user profile (dependency)
 * 2. Soft-delete the created user profile as an authorized actor
 *    - Confirm response contains `id` and `deleted_at` audit fields
 * 3. Attempt to retrieve the deleted profile – verify it is inaccessible (might require a GET endpoint which is assumed here)
 * 4. Attempt to soft-delete a random non-existent profile ID – expect error
 * 5. Attempt to soft-delete a profile with insufficient permissions (simulate by changing identity/context/token) – expect permission error

operations.description:
This endpoint enables creation of a new role entity in the Core schema's roles table. The request body must specify attributes such as organization (ID), name, code, and optional description, adhering to all field and uniqueness constraints on name/code per organization.

Access is highly restricted to actors with administrative privileges. All creation events are audit-logged with full request/response evidence for later compliance or operational investigation. If duplicate names or codes are found within the same organization, the endpoint responds with a conflict error and detailed cause.

Upon successful creation, the endpoint returns the new role object, including all attributes and timestamps. This operation is referenced in onboarding, permissions management, and compliance audit flows for expanded or changed tenant structure.

Upon a successful delete operation, the target session is either soft-deleted (by setting 'revoked_at') or removed according to compliance and evidence preservation requirements. This endpoint is essential for logout or forced session termination scenarios, especially in response to anomalous activity, consent withdrawal, or administrative actions.

Proper permission checks are enforced: end-users may delete only their own active sessions, while admins may remove sessions system-wide. The operation ensures non-repudiation through audit logging in the 'access_logs' and 'audit_log' entities. All session revocations cascade updates to any related authentication tokens, and immediate access loss is enforced system-wide.

Error handling covers cases such as non-existent session IDs, unauthorized access, or attempts to delete already revoked or expired sessions. The response confirms the operation result, with details for compliance and client UX.

operations.description:
This operation permanently deletes a single catalog event entry as identified by the provided unique identifier 'id'. This endpoint is used in rare cases where regulatory compliance, correction of erroneous entries, or explicit business approval authorizes event deletion.

The catalog_events entity, as specified in the schema, is an immutable log—delete is allowed only under strict circumstances (such as GDPR or evidence purge) and must be fully audited. Deletion attempts are logged with before/after data snapshots in the audit log to ensure non-repudiation. No cascading or related catalog change occurs; this only removes the specific event.

A valid UUID is required for the 'id' parameter, which must match an existing catalog_events record. Error handling is strict: 404 for non-existent records, 409 for deletion-conflict, and 403 for insufficient permissions. This operation should be accompanied by security event logging.

Use only in conjunction with compliance/evidence removal workflows, as this may weaken audit trails if misused.

- 모든 API 호출 request body에 타입 만족(satisfies ...) 적용 → 타입 오류 없음. 
- 할인 entity, 페이지 결과 모두 typia.assert로 런타임 검증 진행.

3. **비즈니스 플로우**:
- 테스트 데이터 3건 이상을 동적으로 생성하여, 이후 필터링/페이지 조건 등을 실제 객체 ID, 값 등을 기준으로 검색 → 현실적.

- 변수명, 주석, 코드 포맷 모두 가독성 양호.
- 불필요한 임의 타입 변환/타입 우회 없음.

- notes 검색 지원은 실제 API와 DTO명세 반영 수준 고려.

**Step-by-step review of the draft implementation for the communicationReview domain e2e test:**

- The function has a descriptive docstring explaining the business scenario and test logic for the review moderation event creation endpoint.
- Workflow covers both positive and negative paths: valid creation, missing required field (rationale), bad UUID format, and duplicate submission.
- Correct TypeScript types are used throughout (IReviewModeration.ICreate for creation input, typia.random for valid uuid strings).
- API responses are asserted with typia.assert and cross-checked for property equality against input.
- Error paths use TestValidator.error and code structure/documentation is clear.
- The only minor issue is use of `as any` force-casting types for negative tests (to purposely submit invalid requests). However, per current E2E system guidelines, negative tests must not intentionally break type contracts—so those should be omitted or rewritten to only test runtime errors with valid types.

dto.src/api/structures/IFavoritesPersonaliza:
import { tags } from "typia";

export namespace IFavoritesPersonalization {
  /**
   * Payload for creating a new favorite in the
   * FavoritesPersonalization.favorites table.
   *
   * Encapsulates the data required to establish a user-product favorite
   * relationship, supporting evidence-based insertion, audit, and AI
   * feedback. This is subject to constraints for data integrity and composite
   * uniqueness (user + product). All fields are validated and consent/audit
   * protocols enforced per requirements.
   *
   * Initial creation event is recorded in the evidence/audit log with a
   * non-repudiable entry.
   */
  export type IFavoriteCreate = {
    /**
     * Reference to the user marking the favorite (users.id).
     *
     * User consent and ID validation is enforced for privacy and
     * personalization rights.
     */
    user_id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

    /**
     * Reference to the product being favorited (products.id).
     *
     * Enforces traceable, unique favorite creation and ensures inference in
     * downstream personalization models.
     */
    product_id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;
  };

  /**
   * Represents a user's product favorite entry within the Favorites &
   * Personalization module.
   *
   * This object tracks the explicit action of a user marking a product as a
   * favorite, encapsulating the user-product relationship for auditing and
   * evidence-based personalization. Every record is immutable upon creation
   * save for the logical deletion attribute (deleted_at), in compliance with
   * audit trails, regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA), and data integrity
   * mandates from the requirements analysis and Prisma schema documentation.
   *
   * A favorite cannot be created multiple times per user-product pair (see
   * composite unique constraint), and all operations are logged for
   * explainability and AI feedback cycles in accordance with advanced
   * AI-native requirements.
   */
  export type IFavorite = {
    /**
     * A globally unique identifier for this favorite entry.
     *
     * References the primary key and audit evidence for compliance and
     * analytics. Prisma: favorites.id
     */
    id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

    /**
     * References the user who marked the favorite (users.id FK).
     *
     * Required for evidence preservation, consent management, and
     * compliance auditor queries. Prisma: favorites.user_id
     */
    user_id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

    /**
     * References the product marked as favorite (products.id FK).
     *
     * Enables traceable linkage between user intent and catalog entity for
     * AI/analytics and evidence archiving. Prisma: favorites.product_id
     */
    product_id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

    /**
     * Timestamp for when the favorite was created (UTC, RFC3339).
     *
     * Preserves audit and evidence for timeline analytics, privacy
     * dashboard, and regulatory compliance. Prisma: favorites.created_at
     */
    created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;

    /**
     * Timestamp for soft-delete, or null if the favorite is active.
     *
     * Part of evidence preservation, right-to-be-forgotten, and audit
     * compliance chain. Prisma: favorites.deleted_at.
     */
    deleted_at?: (string & tags.Format<"date-time">) | null;
  };
}

## 코드 리뷰 및 품질 점검

### 1. 비즈니스 로직 및 시나리오 테스트
- 실제 AI decision log의 update가 제대로 작동하는지 검증
- 존재하지 않는 ID에 대해 적절한 에러 발생 확인
- 잘못된 데이터(rationale값이 type 오류 등)에 대해 런타임 에러 메시지 발생 확인
- DTO/엔티티의 불변 필드는 업데이트 이후에도 동일함을 assert로 점검

### 2. TypeScript 타입 안전성 및 샘플 데이터 적합성
- typia.random을 통한 uuid 및 기타 랜덤값 생성: 타입 적합성 유지
- rationale 등 업데이트 가능한 필드만 변경 (불변 evidence필드는 불변 보장 체크)
- 불변 필드 변경 X, IUpdate DTO 준수, 타입 안전성 위반 우회 사용 금지

### 3. Assertion 및 예외 핸들링
- TestValidator.equals로 업데이트된 rationale 및 불변필드 동일성 보장

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Result object for delete, deactivation, or archival operations across all
 * entities.
 *
 * Used as a standardized return value for deletes on evidence-preserving APIs
 * in advanced commerce, AI, or compliance modules. Reports status and deleted
 * ID for evidence chain.
 *
 * Provides legal and forensic trace for destructive, archival, or removal
 * workflows.
 *
 * Generic; referenced across modules, not just in AI logs.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IDeletionResult = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier of the entity logically/physically deleted.
   *
   * Traces directly to primary key of deleted record.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * Describes the outcome of the delete operation for audit purposes (e.g.,
   * deleted, archived, not_found, forbidden).
   *
   * Used by compliance/reporting/forensics clients.
   */
  status: string;

  /**
   * Timestamp when the entity was marked deleted/archived. Null for failures
   * or not-deleted status.
   *
   * Critical for evidence queries and investigation.
   */
  deleted_at?: (string & tags.Format<"date-time">) | null;
};

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Result object for delete, deactivation, or archival operations across all
 * entities.
 *
 * Used as a standardized return value for deletes on evidence-preserving APIs
 * in advanced commerce, AI, or compliance modules. Reports status and deleted
 * ID for evidence chain.
 *
 * Provides legal and forensic trace for destructive, archival, or removal
 * workflows.
 *
 * Generic; referenced across modules, not just in AI logs.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IDeletionResult = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier of the entity logically/physically deleted.
   *
   * Traces directly to primary key of deleted record.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * Describes the outcome of the delete operation for audit purposes (e.g.,
   * deleted, archived, not_found, forbidden).
   *
   * Used by compliance/reporting/forensics clients.
   */
  status: string;

  /**
   * Timestamp when the entity was marked deleted/archived. Null for failures
   * or not-deleted status.
   *
   * Critical for evidence queries and investigation.
   */
  deleted_at?: (string & tags.Format<"date-time">) | null;
};

operations.specification: Create a new permission record. Relates to 'permission' table in the SecurityCompliance schema. Allows administrators to register granular permissions (e.g., 'order.edit') for assignment to roles/policies. This endpoint requires validation, audit logging, and is restricted to privileged users. Supports evidence preservation for regulatory and forensic review.
operations.description:
This API endpoint is used to create a new permission in the system, as per the 'permission' schema in the SecurityCompliance module. It requires administrators to specify a unique permission code, human-consumable description, and optional association to a policy (for grouping/rule enforcement).

Permission creation supports RBAC, API security, and evidencing requirements, as stated in the requirements and Prisma schema comments. The implementation matches compliance and explainability mandates by preserving a full audit of the creation event, including the identity of the creating user and timestamp.

Validation: code must be unique and meet format rules; description required and non-empty. Request is rejected if the permission code is already taken. Related operations: get, update, delete; link to policies for policy-driven enforcement.

Security: Only accessible to system admins or privileged operator roles. Logs action to the audit trail for compliance trace. Errors: duplicate entry, validation error.

operations.specification: Update attributes of a single permission record by ID. Operates on the 'permission' table of SecurityCompliance. Allows privileged users to change code, description, or associated policy. Preserves history of all updates for evidence and regulatory audits. Enforces permission code uniqueness and evidence requirements. Access restricted to superuser/admin. Changes are logged for full traceability.
operations.description:
This API allows privileged users (admins) to update an individual permission's attributes, such as its code (must remain unique), human-readable description, or the associated policy. The update reflects directly in the 'permission' entity in the Prisma SecurityCompliance schema.

Every modification is logged via the audit trail for compliance, as mandated in the requirements for fine-grained evidencing and traceability. This endpoint also supports explainability features—enabling changes to permission configuration to be inspected historically. If the permission does not exist, a not-found error is returned. If the code would create a duplicate, a conflict/validation error is thrown.

Only accessible by superuser/admin roles. Related operations: create, get, delete. Errors: not found, forbidden, duplicate code.

operations.specification: Delete a single permission record by ID. Modifies the 'permission' table in SecurityCompliance. Supports soft or hard deletion as per regulatory requirement (typically soft-delete). Restricted to admins/superusers. Deletions are logged for full evidence/audit chain. Not reversible via API. operations.description:
This API operation deletes a specific permission entity identified by its UUID, as per the SecurityCompliance.permission Prisma schema. Deletion is subject to regulatory evidence requirements—typically implemented as a soft-delete (record remains for audit, but is not active or assignable).

Deleting a permission restricts its assignment to roles/policies, immediately affecting RBAC and dynamic policy checks throughout the system. The operation must be performed by a privileged user (admin/superuser) and triggers an audit log for full evidence preservation.

Error handling: returns not-found if entity does not exist or already deleted, forbidden for insufficient privileges. Deleted entity info is included in the response for compliance and forensics.
